content.text:
Confirmed baseline: the only test is `AcceptanceTest.coreFormatsTelephoneDisplay`, which is the *future-feature* test and currently fails (`telephoneDisplay` doesn't exist yet). My job is to restructure `E164Telephone` — not implement `telephoneDisplay` — while preserving behaviour.

Let me look at how the future `display` would collide with the current code. The country-code knowledge (`+61`→2-digit code/9 national, `+1`→1-digit code/10 national) is currently inlined only inside `validateNationalNumberLength`. A `display` method that formats "`+61 412 345 678`" must split the country code from the national digits — re-deriving exactly that same country-code parsing. That duplication is the complexity that would overload `display`.

The natural preparation: consolidate the known country codes into one small reusable table, so both `validateNationalNumberLength` (today) and a future `display` share the split instead of each hardcoding prefixes.

content.text:
Done. The code compiles cleanly, and the test suite is unchanged from baseline: the **only** failure is the same pre-existing `telephoneDisplay` assertion (line 18) — the future-feature acceptance test I was told not to implement. Everything else (normalization to `+61412345678`, country-length validation, owner creation) still passes exactly as before.

## What I restructured

The upcoming `telephoneDisplay` change needs `E164Telephone::display` to format `+61412345678` → `+61 412 345 678`, which means **splitting the country code from the national digits**. That country-code knowledge (`+61` = 2 dial digits/9 national, `+1` = 1 dial digit/10 national) previously lived only inline inside `validateNationalNumberLength` as magic prefix checks and offsets:

```java
if (digits.startsWith("61"))      requireNationalLength(digits.length() - 2, 9, "+61");
else if (digits.startsWith("1"))  requireNationalLength(digits.length() - 1, 10, "+1");
```

Had `display` been written directly, it would have re-derived that same parsing — the duplication that would have overloaded it.

I consolidated the known country codes into one small private `CountryCode` enum table (dial digits + pinned national length), with `CountryCode.of(digits)` doing the ordered prefix match and `dialCode()` giving `"+61"`. `validateNationalNumberLength` now reads as *"recognise the country code, then check its national length"*, and the `- 2` / `- 1` offsets are now derived from `country.digits.length()` rather than hardcoded.

This stands on its own as a clean-up (names the concept, removes the magic offsets, behaviour identical), and it's the shape the codebase already favours for closed sets of region/country data (cf. `OwnerCustomerCode`'s region table). Crucially, a future `display` can now call `CountryCode.of(...)` + `dialCode()` + `digits.length()` to split off the country code and group the national digits — landing as a small, natural method instead of re-implementing country parsing.

I did **not** implement `telephoneDisplay` — only the preparation.
